question_or_symptom: The ninth client was intended to receive RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, but an accept-time one-shot read could close it before HELLO arrived and could not run during gem5's blocking startup wait.
observation: Connection establishment and the first SOCK_SEQPACKET record are separate readiness events. Scheduling one nonblocking recv immediately after accept makes EAGAIN a race-dependent close, while a queued gem5 event is not serviced during the startup wall-clock wait.
conclusion: A bounded rejection client is still a protocol client and must use the same readiness, deadline, ancillary cleanup, and partial-send state machine as an admitted client.
decision: Track eight regular and eight resource-limited clients with independent admission counters. Both classes receive PollEvent and timerfd ownership plus nonblocking outbound retry; negotiation marks limited clients RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The real gate exercises an immediate ninth HELLO during startup and a ninth connection held idle before HELLO in steady state, then proves slot and file-descriptor recovery.
invalidated_assumptions: A client that exceeds the regular capacity will always have sent HELLO by the first accept callback.
An event scheduled at tick zero is serviced while startup is blocked in an external poll loop.
